sections.text: You're listening to the Skeptics' Guide to the Universe, your escape to reality.
sections.title: Introduction

sections.text: In a recent discussion with my girlfriend about prayer I asked her to 'give me one single instance where she could demonstrate that a prayer was actually answered'. She, of course, had no real answer but responded that 'not everything real is scientific'. How can I respond to that? Can something be 'real' and not 'scientific'. Jim McDowell USA
Sharon Begley is the science news editor for Newsweek Magazine.
sections.title: Interview with Sharon Begley

sections.text:
Item #1: A recent survey shows that online gamers are more physically fit than the general population
Item #2: Astronomers have discovered a new class of neutron star, called a gravitar, which is more massive than the previously calculated upper limit for neutron stars.
Item #3: A recent nutritional survey shows that most children are getting more than enough vitamins and minerals in their diet.
sections.title: Science or Fiction

sections.text: '...I think the popular view of Science is a solid body of truth, shared by a whole lot of learned men in a room, all agreeing on the answers to the questions of how the Universe works. Whereas nothing could be further from the truth !!! The one truth that I see emerging from the History of Science is that experiment has always surprised theorists. Einstein included!' - Dr. Brian May
